strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, each preceded by local computation of scaling factors from the previous result. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches with full 2048-element payloads. Represents the straightforward implementation with maximal latency but simplest control flow.

strategies.name: Block-Parallel Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather
strategies.desc: Splits each iteration into reduce-scatter (8 blocks distributed across ranks) followed by all-gather to reconstruct full vector, enabling parallelization of per-block scaling computations. Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on 1/world_size payload, trading dispatch count for reduced per-dispatch bandwidth and exploiting block independence.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped All-Reduce with Async
strategies.desc: Issues next all-reduce asynchronously while computing scaling factors for current result, overlapping communication with computation across the 8 iterations. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but pipeline-fills to hide computation latency behind network transfers, optimizing for wall-clock time on high-latency interconnects.

strategies.name: Fused Multi-Block All-Reduce with Vectorized Local Ops
strategies.desc: Packs all 8 blocks into single tensors and fuses local operations (squaring, mean, scaling) using vectorized torch operations before each all-reduce, minimizing kernel launch overhead. Maintains 8 all-reduce dispatches but drastically reduces local compute overhead through batched operations and better memory locality.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction with Intra-Node Fusion
strategies.desc:
Exploits multi-node topology by first performing intra-node reductions (across cores_per_device × num_devices) using shared memory, then inter-node all-reduce, repeated for 8 iterations. Uses 16 total dispatches (8 intra-node + 8 inter-node) but leverages faster intra-node bandwidth and reduces cross-node traffic by factor of ranks-per-node.
